topic: The Emu War of 1932 in Western Australia
The Pig War of 1859: the United States and Britain nearly went to war on San Juan Island after a farmer shot a pig
The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 27 August 1896, the shortest war in recorded history
my_take: This war was shorter than my tea break. Some of my office meetings last longer than this whole war!

topic: The Great Moon Hoax of 1835: the New York Sun's articles about life on the Moon
my_take: In eighteen thirty-five, people believed in bat-men on the Moon. Today we have WhatsApp forwards. Honestly, not much has changed!

topic: Mike the Headless Chicken, who lived about 18 months without most of his head (1945-1947)
my_take: My take: Mike lived for eighteen months without a head. On Monday mornings, I feel exactly like Mike!

topic: Acoustic Kitty: the CIA's 1960s project to turn a cat into a listening device
my_take: The CIA spent a fortune to turn a cat into a spy. Anyone who owns a cat could have told them: cats never do what you ask!

topic: The exploding whale of 1970: Oregon highway workers blew up a dead sperm whale on the beach at Florence with dynamite, and blubber rained down on the watching crowd
Wojtek, the brown bear who was enlisted in the Polish army in the Second World War, carried ammunition crates and became a corporal
The dancing plague of 1518 in Strasbourg (say which details historians dispute)

Sergeant Stubby, the stray dog who went to the First World War with American soldiers, warned them of gas attacks and was honoured as a war hero
Tulip mania in the Dutch Republic (1630s), when tulip bulbs sold for huge prices
The Great Stink of London in 1858 and how it got the city its sewers
Project Pigeon: the psychologist B. F. Skinner's Second World War plan to have trained pigeons steer missiles by pecking at a screen
